root_causes: Inefficient policy behavior: despite the task being simple (move a single known object to a target receptacle), the agents spent many steps repeatedly executing low-information actions (Wait and Explore) instead of quickly transitioning to pick-and-place.

Poor termination/efficiency criterion: the controller allowed the episode to run to 96 simulation steps with only 1 planning step, leading to excessive exploration/idle behavior even though the task was ultimately completed.
Suboptimal multi-agent role allocation: Agent 0 remained stationary (repeated Wait actions) rather than being assigned a complementary or backup role, effectively wasting available capabilities.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce an explicit efficiency objective or step budget that encourages the planner/policy to minimize steps once the object and target receptacle are known, reducing unnecessary Wait/Explore cycles.
Improve the action-selection policy to transition more aggressively from exploration to manipulation once the sushi mat is localized, prioritizing Pick/Place over continued Explore in the same room.
Enhance termination conditions so that once the success condition is achieved and verified, the episode ends promptly instead of continuing with redundant steps.
Implement better multi-agent coordination, e.g., assigning Agent 0 to assist with navigation, object search, or as a fallback manipulator instead of idling with repeated Wait actions.
overall_assessment: The task was completed successfully but with significant inefficiency due to unnecessary exploration and idle behavior, especially given the simplicity of moving a single known object. Execution quality is functionally correct but suboptimal in terms of step and resource usage.
task_instruction: Move the sushi mat from the kitchen counter to the living room table.
